intro.data: The target world here is unlabeled — P, Q, R, with arrows u : P→Q and w : Q→R. You can't read off where each thing goes; you must DEDUCE it. A functor must send every source arrow to a target arrow with matching ends, so the objects can only line up one way. Map the chain.
intro.alchemy: The target world is unlabeled — P, Q, R with arrows u : P→Q and w : Q→R. Deduce the mapping: every source arrow must land on a target arrow with matching ends. Map the chain.
intro.spellcraft: The target world is unlabeled — P, Q, R with arrows u : P→Q and w : Q→R. Deduce the mapping: every source arrow must land on a target arrow with matching ends. Map the chain.
intro.abstract: The target is unlabeled (P, Q, R; u : P→Q, w : Q→R). Deduce the functor: every source arrow must land on a target arrow with matching ends.

goal.data: Map the chain A → B → C onto its Optional version so both steps still connect.
goal.alchemy: Map the chain A → B → C onto its Trace version so both steps still connect.
goal.spellcraft: Map the chain A → B → C onto its Echo version so both steps still connect.
goal.abstract: Map A, B, C and f, g so every arrow's endpoints are preserved.

afterSuccess.data: You deduced the whole mapping from the arrows alone — no labels needed. Because each arrow's ends are fixed, the objects could only line up one way; swap the middle and a step would have nowhere to land. A functor must respect every arrow.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You deduced the whole mapping from the arrows alone. Each arrow's ends are fixed, so the objects line up only one way. A functor must respect every arrow.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You deduced the whole mapping from the arrows alone. Each arrow's ends are fixed, so the objects line up only one way. A functor must respect every arrow.
afterSuccess.abstract: You deduced the mapping from the arrows alone. Each arrow's ends are fixed, so the objects line up only one way — a functor must respect every arrow. (And many functors can exist between the same two categories.)

reveal.summary: A functor must preserve every arrow's source and target, so the object and morphism assignments have to agree. Different functors (List, Optional, …) give different — but all valid — maps.
reveal.moreFormal: There is usually more than one functor C → D. Each is a complete, structure-preserving copy of C inside D; the identity functor and constant functors are always available too.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: Both List and Optional are functors with their own map; you pick which world to map into.
